name: Taanach
overview: Taanach was a significant city in the land allotted to the tribe of Manasseh, yet the Israelites did not fully drive out the Canaanite inhabitants, allowing them to remain in the land (Joshua 17:12; Judges 1:27). It was also assigned as a Levitical city within the half tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 21:25). Taanach is noted as a strategic location where the kings of Canaan fought, marking the scene of Barak's victory, and it served as one of Solomon's commissaries (Judges 5:19; Joshua 12:21). These facts illustrate the city's enduring importance in Israel's history and God's unfolding plan for His people.
